title: Add MXFP4 -> FP8 expert checkpoint conversion for SM90 (Hopper)
body:
### Motivation

The released V4.1-Flash checkpoint stores routed experts as MXFP4 (packed e2m1 + per-row UE8M0 scales), which requires SM100 FP4 tensor cores. Hopper (SM90 — e.g. H20, the most widely deployed inference GPU in mainland China) has no FP4 support, so a converted FP8-expert checkpoint is the prerequisite for every later SM90 step.

This PR adds the offline conversion tooling and the config-side acceptance. It is the first piece of the SM90 work; the FP8-expert loading branch in `_load_expert_params` follows separately.

### What's included

**`scripts/convert_mxfp4_to_fp8.py`** — standalone (torch + safetensors only, runs on a CPU box, no DeepInfer build):

- expert weights `...ffn.experts.{e}.w{1,2,3}.weight`: packed e2m1 int8 `(n, k//2)` + UE8M0 scales `(n, k//32)` → dequantized FP32 → requantized **F8_E4M3 `(n, k)` with per-32×32-block scales** (amax → 448, unit scale for zero blocks);
- expert scales `...scale`: become **FP32 `(n//32, k//32)` row-major** — requantized block scales are not powers of two, so they cannot stay in F8_E8M0 without corrupting them;
- everything else (attention/shared-expert FP8 weights and their F8_E8M0 scales, Engram tables, tokenizer) is copied byte-identically; shards are processed one at a time to bound host memory;
- `config.json` is rewritten with `quantization_config.expert_dtype: "fp8"` and (unless `--keep-fp4-kv`) `text_config.use_fp4_sparse_kv: false` — the FP8 main-KV runtime path (`V41_FORMAT`) already exists end to end;
- e2m1 nibble order defaults to low-nibble-first (the OCP MXFP4 / DeepGEMM convention) with `--high-nibble-first` as the escape hatch; it should be validated once against `tile_kernels.quant.per_token_cast` on a real GPU.

**`deepinfer/hugging_face/config.py`** — the quantization validation now accepts `expert_dtype` `"fp8"` in addition to `"fp4"` (anything else is still rejected). `mxfp4=False` then flows into the existing runtime path: `mlp.py` derives `mma_type="fp8xfp8"` and `process_moe_weight(use_fp4=False)` already handles the FP8 layout. Note `bf16` experts are *not* accepted: `quant_method` must be `"fp8"`, so activations are always FP8 and `bf16xbf16` can never be selected.

**`tests/test_convert_mxfp4.py`** — 11 CPU-only unit tests: e2m1 LUT and decode against an independent reference encoder (both nibble orders), lossless UE8M0→FP32, requantization error bounds (2⁻⁴ relative + e4m3 subnormal granularity), zero-block handling, shape rejection, and an end-to-end miniature checkpoint conversion (shapes/dtypes, passthrough byte-equality of ordinary weights, config rewrite, `--keep-fp4-kv`).

### What is deliberately not in this PR

- **The FP8-expert loader branch** (`_load_expert_params` currently hard-asserts the packed-FP4 3D int8 layout). The output format defined here — per-expert F8_E4M3 `(n, k)` + FP32 `(n//32, k//32)` `.scale`, w1/w3 concatenated along dim 0 for `linear1` — is the contract that branch will read.
- `platform.py` `fp8_sf_type` parameterization and the DeepGEMM SM90 (`disable_ue8m0_cast=True`) dispatch, which only matter once loading works.

Tracked in the SM90 series (H20 141GB target); the format contract above is the reference for the follow-up loader PR.
